preconditions.expression: all('a' <= c <= 'z' or 'A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in S) and all('a' <= c <= 'z' or 'A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in P)
preconditions.description: Both strings S and P consist only of alphabetic characters (case-sensitive).
Lengths of S and P are between 1 and 60 inclusive.
The length of P must be exactly twice the length of S (since P is formed by inserting a copy of S into S).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Possible' if any(P[:i] + S + P[i:] == P and P[i:i+len(S)] == S for i in range(len(S) + 1)) else 'Impossible'
postconditions.description: The output is 'Possible' if and only if P can be formed by inserting a copy of S into S exactly once at some position i (0 ≤ i ≤ len(S)). This means P must be equal to the concatenation of the first i characters of S, followed by S, followed by the remaining characters of S (from i to end).
